description: Create a new module. Supports workflow modules (states, activities, flows) and record list modules (fields only). Requires Administrator, Consultant, or Workspace Admin role. Validates internally with the same rules as validate_design and returns structured errors without creating anything — a separate validate_design call beforehand is optional. See inistate://schema/configure for field types, color palette, and design rules. A new module is open to everyone in the workspace until set_module_access restricts it.

activities.description: Custom activities. Omit for record list modules.

actor.description: Who performs the activity when an AI is asked to: ai — the AI submits it; hybrid — the user approves the planned submission first; human — a person performs it. Studio and the TeamMate call these Performs, Asks first and Human only: a user asking for "Asks first" means hybrid. Omitted, a workflow activity is hybrid (Asks first); set human for one only a person may perform.

confidence_threshold.description: 0-1; values above 1 are read as percent

readOnlyWhen.description: The field is read-only on this form while this holds: a true/false condition in the "=" syntax with display names, e.g. "={{form.Type}} = \"Travel\"" or "={{form.Amount}} > 1000". "" removes it; omit to keep it. get_module_canvas shows it as written; send it back unchanged to keep it.

requiredWhen.description: The field is required on this form while this holds: a true/false condition in the "=" syntax with display names, e.g. "={{form.Type}} = \"Travel\"" or "={{form.Amount}} > 1000". "" removes it; omit to keep it. get_module_canvas shows it as written; send it back unchanged to keep it.

visibleWhen.description: The form shows this field only while this holds: a true/false condition in the "=" syntax with display names, e.g. "={{form.Type}} = \"Travel\"" or "={{form.Amount}} > 1000". "" removes it; omit to keep it. get_module_canvas shows it as written; send it back unchanged to keep it.

humanWhen.description: Human only when — on an ai or hybrid activity, a true/false condition that makes it human-only for the values it holds for, e.g. "{{form.Amount}} > 10000". Name fields as {{form.Field Name}} (submitted values over stored) or {{entry.Field Name}} (as stored). "" removes it; omit to keep it. Removing or rewriting one needs a person: the write answers design_approval_required (confirmed: true does not pass it), and only if the user says so, send it again with approval.

ai.description: REQUIRED — why the design changes, kept in the module's history. Not the module's description.

reasoning.description: Why the design changes this way — the change note kept in the module's history (≤ 2000 chars). One or two sentences naming the decision, e.g. "Added Discount because quotes over 10k need a negotiated price".

request.description: A short paraphrase of what the user asked for (≤ 500 chars). No personal data beyond what the design needs.

sources.description: Evidence for the change: {type: user_message | entry | document | url | module, reference, excerpt}. References as ids or URLs.

approval.description: ONLY after the user asked for it: send a change that answered design_approval_required to a person instead of saving it. They review it in Studio on the web and approve (the platform then saves exactly this design as them) or reject. Nothing is saved now: the answer says performed: false with a requestId; tell the user, and read the outcome with get_approval_request when they ask. Send the same payload that was refused, with approval added.

expiresIn.description: How long it stays open: "30m", "72h" or "3d"; default 72h, at most 14d

recipients.description: Usernames of design admins who may approve (max 10); omit for the user you act for. A workspace whose design approvals need a different person answers approver_required when no one else is named: ask the user who should approve, then send again with their username

summary.description: Why, for the approver, in one or two sentences (max 500 characters); defaults to ai.reasoning

card.description: The listing card designed with the schema — how each entry shows in the module's list (mobile and web). Fields and activities by NAME. See CardDefinition in inistate://schema/configure. A card that does not pass never fails the call: the module gets the platform's default card and the response's cardStatus says why.

action.description: 'view' (the default when activities exist), 'edit', or an activity name

field.description: An Image, Images, File, Files or Selection field, by name

size.description: XS | S | M | L (S for a Selection, M for an image)

rows.description: 1–5 rows of 1–3 items: the state row first (or the defaultCard widget alone), the title field L/b, secondary fields S/M, activities in their own row

name.description: Field or activity name; 'defaultCard' for the widget; unused for state

settings.description: defaultCard widget switches (booleans): title, state, assignees, comment, createdBy, createdDate, due, documentId

size.description: S | M | L — Text, number and date fields only

style.description: l | n | b — Text, number and date fields only

type.description: 'grid' when the module has an Image/Images field (the image alone in row 1); otherwise 'detail' with an icon

description.description: The module's own description, shown to its users. Not a change note: say why you changed the design in ai.reasoning.

documentIdFormat.description: The document number every new entry gets: plain text around the serial {0} (or {0:D5} for five digits with leading zeros), the entry's date {1:yyMM} (y, M and d with - / . or _ between) and a field's value {field('Field Name')}, e.g. "EC-{1:yyMM}-{0:D4}". The serial must be in it. Nothing else in braces is taken. "" goes back to the platform's default; omit to keep it. The response's documentIdExample shows the number it makes.

dryRun.description: Not here: create_module always creates. validate_design checks a new design without creating it.

flows.description: State transition rules: { from, to, activity } by name. Omit for record list modules.

information.description: Field definitions. Items matched by id on update enable renaming.

connection.description: Name of an existing module in this workspace to link to. Required for User/Users/Module/Modules types.

display.description: User/Users/Module/Modules only: name of the connected module's field shown for a picked record. Omit to default (Full Name/Name for users, else the first Text field).

connection.description: Module columns only: name of an existing module in this workspace each row links one record of (e.g. "Products" for line items). Modules, User and Users columns are not offered inside a table.

display.description: Module columns only: name of the connected module's field shown for a picked record. Omit to default (the first Text field).

formula.description: The column's value on each row as a formula, making it a computed column: worked out on every row on every submit (submit_activity included, so leave it out of the rows you send), and read-only on every form. Name the row's own columns through the table, e.g. "={{form.Lines.Qty}} * {{form.Lines.Price}}". A field's formula can total it: "=SUM({{form.Lines.Amount}})". "" makes it an ordinary column again; omit to keep it.

The field's value as a formula, making it a computed field: worked out on every submit of every activity and read-only on every form. Write it in the "=" syntax with display names, e.g. "=SUM({{form.Lines.Amount}})" or "={{form.Price}} * {{form.Quantity}}". "" makes it an ordinary field again; omit to keep it. get_module_canvas shows it as written; send it back unchanged to keep it.

profile.description: Make it a people module: one entry per member, linked by the built-in Username field (name 'Username' in an activity's fields; the standard Create, Edit and View forms carry it). Its fields — e.g. a Position selection — are what position grants in set_module_access read. Create only.

states.description: Workflow states. Omit for record list modules.

color.description: Palette: #5A6070 #2968A8 #2A7B50 #A07828 #C0392B #6B4D91 #1E6B45 #8B2D2D. Names ('red', 'amber') and other hex are normalized to the nearest.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID for this call. The MCP keeps no workspace between calls, so pass it every time; omit only when INISTATE_WORKSPACE_ID is configured.

name: create_module
title: Create Module
